title: When Helping Hurts: How to Alleviate Poverty Without Hurting the Poor . . . and Yourself
author: Steve Corbett and Brian Fikkert
target_audience: Church leaders and members involved in missions or outreach
Individuals interested in effective poverty alleviation
Students of social work or development studies
core_themes: Critical evaluation of Western approaches to aid
primary_purpose: To challenge and guide Christians and faith-based organizations to engage in poverty alleviation efforts that truly help the poor and avoid approaches that inadvertently cause harm; it emphasizes building relationships and empowering local communities rather than fostering dependency through misguided charity.

structure_format.narrative_style: Conversational with theological and practical guidance
structure_format.organization: Divided into three main sections: foundational concepts, practical applications, and specific ministry scenarios

key_concepts_lessons: Poverty is more than material lack; it is rooted in broken relationships with God, self, others, and creation.
Western approaches to poverty alleviation often impose solutions and create dependency rather than empowerment.
There is a crucial difference between relief (immediate aid), rehabilitation (restoration), and development (ongoing progress), and each is appropriate in different contexts.
Effective poverty alleviation involves listening to, learning from, and partnering with the poor rather than doing for them.
Asset-based community development builds on existing capabilities within communities.
Short-term missions and handouts can be harmful if not structured thoughtfully and respectfully.
notable_features: Widely used by churches and Christian organizations for training and group study
Focus on biblically grounded, sustainable strategies
Clear distinction between types of aid (relief, rehabilitation, development)
Discussion questions and group resources included
Real-life stories illustrate both effective and counterproductive efforts
cultural_historical_context: Emerging from growing concerns in the early 21st century about the unintended downsides of Western charity, particularly in Christian circles, the book reflects a shift toward more sustainable, dignity-focused approaches to poverty alleviation both domestically and globally.
reception_impact: Highly influential in North American Christian missions and charity
Praised for changing mindsets and practices in church-based poverty work
Regularly adopted in ministry training programs
Critics note a strong theological focus may limit broader secular application
comparable_titles: Toxic Charity: How Churches and Charities Hurt Those They Help (And How to Reverse It) by Robert D. Lupton
The Hole in Our Gospel by Richard Stearns
When Helping Hurts: The Small Group Experience by Steve Corbett and Brian Fikkert
Walking with the Poor: Principles and Practices of Transformational Development by Bryant L. Myers
